action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Machine
2	
3	/-!
4	# Corpus MM2-H on the memory machine (test module, spec v0 Parts II–III, §8–§20)
5	
6	Test module. It states no semantics: it runs the MM2-H corpus (non-normative validation
7	material, 17 identifiers, H13 split into H13a and H13b, 18 scenarios) on the relations of
8	`Ern.MemoryModel.Machine`.
9	
10	Each case gives a state reached from the empty state, an admissible initial state (§9 ¶9), by an
11	execution of `ok` steps (`Exec`, §20.3 ¶3), and the outcome of the normative relation at that
12	state (`ReadStep`, `WriteStep`, `DeallocStep`, `AllocStep`, §20.1), proved by `decide` or by the
13	machine lemmas. Each `ub` case has a separate `_twin` theorem for the corpus's positive twin.
14	The docstring of each theorem states the expected verdict from the corpus, the obtained verdict,
15	and the class (rule "classement" of the corpus: `N2` = memory machine). Where the obtained
16	verdict differs from the expected one, the docstring says "Mismatch" and the case is kept as
17	written, not corrected.
18	
19	Context of every execution (§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3: explicit context parameters): compatibility is
20	equality of the presented authority with the recorded token (§17 ¶4); read and write
21	obligations are the machine's explicit test instances `Witness.obR` and `Witness.obW` (both parts
22	`True`), except in H14, which needs a false static part.
23	
24	Open obligations, not declared passed: H10 address formation (§14 ¶4, §19), H13a at language
25	level (§10 ¶4, §19), H13b (§19).
26	-/
27	
28	namespace Ern.Corpus.MM2H
29	
30	open Ern.MemoryModel.Machine
31	
32	/-! ## Run builders -/
33	
34	section Builders
35	
36	variable {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {W : WriteOblSpec Ty}
37	
38	/-- An execution extended by one `ok` step at its end is an execution (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). -/
39	theorem exec_snoc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {op : Op Ty} {s₀ s s' : State}
40	    (h : Exec C R W ops s₀ s) (hs : Step C R W op s s') : Exec C R W (ops ++ [op]) s₀ s' := by
41	  induction h with
42	  | nil => exact .cons hs (.nil _)
43	  | cons h₀ _ ih => exact .cons h₀ (ih hs)
44	
45	/-- Appending an `ok` raw creation to an execution from the empty state. The decidable form
46	`AllocPreDec` suffices because every reached state satisfies freshness (§9 ¶7, §9 ¶9, §9 ¶11). -/
47	theorem run_alloc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
48	    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
49	    (hp : AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
50	    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.alloc space base size align freeAuth]) State.empty
51	      (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth) :=
52	  exec_snoc h (.alloc (.ok ((allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).1 hp)))
53	
54	/-- Appending an `ok` raw write to an execution from the empty state (§16, §20.2 ¶2). -/
55	theorem run_write {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
56	    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hc : CanWrite s ac)
57	    (hd : W.dec s ac t w) (hs : W.stat s ac t w) :
58	    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.write ac t w]) State.empty (s.write ac w) :=
59	  exec_snoc h (.write (.ok ⟨hc, hd, hs⟩))
60	
61	/-- Appending an `ok` raw deallocation to an execution from the empty state (§17, §20.2 ¶2). -/
62	theorem run_dealloc {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {id auth : Nat}
63	    (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hc : CanDealloc C s id auth) :
64	    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.dealloc id auth]) State.empty (s.dealloc id) :=
65	  exec_snoc h (.dealloc (.ok hc))
66	
67	/-- Appending an `ok` raw read to an execution from the empty state; the state is unchanged
68	(§15, §20.2 ¶1). -/
69	theorem run_read {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {v : List AByte}
70	    (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s) (hr : ReadStep R ac t s (.ok v)) :
71	    Exec C R W (ops ++ [.read ac t]) State.empty s :=
72	  exec_snoc h (.read hr)
73	
74	/-- At a state reached from the empty state, a creation whose decidable preconditions fail is
75	`ub` (§9 ¶11, §20.1 ¶2). -/
76	theorem allocStep_ub {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
77	    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
78	    (hn : ¬ AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
79	    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s .ub :=
80	  .ub (mt (allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).2 hn)
81	
82	/-- At a state reached from the empty state, a creation whose decidable preconditions hold is
83	`ok` with the creation effect (§9 ¶11, §20.1 ¶2). -/
84	theorem allocStep_ok {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s : State} {space base size align : Nat}
85	    {freeAuth : Option Nat} (h : Exec C R W ops State.empty s)
86	    (hp : AllocPreDec s space base size align) :
87	    AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth)) :=
88	  .ok ((allocPreDec_iff (h.admissible admissible_empty).wf).1 hp)
89	
90	end Builders
91	
92	/-! ## Context and common states -/
93	
94	/-- Read obligations of the corpus context: the machine's explicit test instance, both parts
95	`True` (§20.3 ¶1). -/
96	abbrev ctxR : ReadOblSpec Unit := Witness.obR.toSpec
97	
98	/-- Write obligations of the corpus context: the machine's explicit test instance, both parts
99	`True` (§20.3 ¶1). -/
100	abbrev ctxW : WriteOblSpec Unit := Witness.obW.toSpec
101	
102	/-- Executions of the corpus context from the empty state (§9 ¶9, §20.3 ¶3): compatibility is
103	equality of presented authority and recorded token (§17 ¶2, §17 ¶4), obligations `ctxR`,
104	`ctxW`. -/
105	abbrev Run (ops : List (Op Unit)) (s : State) : Prop :=
106	  Exec (· = ·) ctxR ctxW ops State.empty s
107	
108	/-- A read whose interpreter result is `o` has the relational outcome `o` (§20.3 ¶3, by
109	`read_sound`). -/
110	theorem readStep_of {ac : Access} {s : State} {o : ReadOutcome}
111	    (h : read Witness.obR ac () s trivial = o) : ReadStep ctxR ac () s o :=
112	  read_sound h
113	
114	/-- Write access to `[96, 104)` with provenance `p` (§12 ¶1). -/
115	def wr (p : Nat) : Access := ⟨96, p, 8, .write⟩
116	
117	/-- Read access to `[96, 104)` with provenance `p` (§12 ¶1). -/
118	def rd (p : Nat) : Access := ⟨96, p, 8, .read⟩
119	
120	/-- One live allocation: identity `0`, space `0`, base `96`, size `8`, alignment `8`,
121	deallocation token `7` (§9 ¶1, §9 ¶11). -/
122	abbrev a8 : State := State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)
123	
124	/-- `a8` after a write of `Witness.w₀` (value `i + 1`, no provenance) over its whole range
125	(§16 ¶2). -/
126	abbrev a8w : State := a8.write (wr 0) Witness.w₀
127	
128	/-- `a8` after deallocation of allocation `0` (§17 ¶3). -/
129	abbrev a8d : State := a8.dealloc 0
130	
131	/-- The empty state is reached by the empty execution (§9 ¶9). -/
132	theorem run_empty : Run [] State.empty :=
133	  .nil _
134	
135	/-- `a8` is reached by one `ok` creation (§9 ¶11). -/
136	theorem run_a8 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 :=
137	  run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)
138	
139	/-- `a8w` is reached by a creation and an `ok` write (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
140	theorem run_a8w : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w :=
141	  run_write run_a8 (by decide) trivial trivial
142	
143	/-- `a8d` is reached by a creation and an `ok` deallocation (§9 ¶11, §17). -/
144	theorem run_a8d : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d :=
145	  run_dealloc run_a8 (by decide)
146	
147	/-! ## H01 — address reuse after deallocation -/
148	
149	/-- State of H01: `a8w`, deallocation of `0`, then a new allocation at the same base `96`,
150	which receives identity `1` (§13 ¶1, §13 ¶2). -/
151	abbrev h01 : State := (a8w.dealloc 0).alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)
152	
153	/-- Operations reaching `h01` (§9 ¶11, §16, §17). -/
154	abbrev h01Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
155	  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7, .alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)]
156	
157	/-- `h01` is reached, and the new allocation lies at the old base `96` (§13 ¶2). -/
158	theorem run_h01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ∃ b, h01.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 :=
159	  ⟨run_alloc (run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide)) (by decide), _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
160	
161	/-- H01. Free, allocate at the same base, read through the old access. Expected `ub`;
162	obtained `ub`: the old provenance designates the dead allocation `0` (§12 ¶3, §13 ¶2, §15.1,
163	§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
164	theorem H01 : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h01 .ub :=
165	  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
166	
167	/-- H01 twin as written ("read through the new access"). Expected `ok`; obtained `ub`.
168	Mismatch, case defect: the new allocation is wholly uninitialized (§10 ¶5), so a read of
169	length `8` through it violates §15.3. Class N2. -/
170	theorem H01_twin : Run h01Ops h01 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () h01 .ub :=
171	  ⟨run_h01.1, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
172	
173	/-- Variant of the H01 twin, not the corpus's twin: a write through the new access before the
174	read. Obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5). It shows that the `ub` of
175	`H01_twin` comes from §10 ¶5, not from the address reuse. -/
176	theorem H01_twin_variant :
177	    Run (h01Ops ++ [.write (wr 1) () Witness.w₀]) (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) ∧
178	    ReadStep ctxR (rd 1) () (h01.write (wr 1) Witness.w₀) (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
179	  ⟨run_write run_h01.1 (by decide) trivial trivial, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
180	
181	/-! ## H02, H03 — deallocation -/
182	
183	/-- H02. Double deallocation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`: the allocation is dead (§17.1,
184	§17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
185	theorem H02 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
186	    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8d .ub :=
187	  ⟨run_a8d, .ub (by decide)⟩
188	
189	/-- H02 twin: a single deallocation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.1, §17.2). Class N2. -/
190	theorem H02_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
191	  ⟨run_a8, .ok (by decide)⟩
192	
193	/-- H03. Deallocation with an authority (`8`) not compatible with the token (`7`) under the
194	context relation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§17.2, §17 ¶4, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
195	theorem H03 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 8 a8 .ub :=
196	  ⟨run_a8, .ub (by decide)⟩
197	
198	/-- H03 twin: compatible authority `7`. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§17.2). Class N2. -/
199	theorem H03_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8 (.ok a8d) :=
200	  H02_twin
201	
202	/-! ## H04, H05, H06 — read conditions -/
203	
204	/-- H04. Read of uninitialized bytes, right after creation. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
205	(§10 ¶5, §15.3). Class N2. -/
206	theorem H04 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub :=
207	  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
208	
209	/-- H04 twin: write, then read. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the written bytes (§16 ¶2,
210	§16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
211	theorem H04_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
212	    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) :=
213	  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
214	
215	/-- H05. Read of `[101, 105)`, one byte past the end `104`. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub`
216	(§15 ¶1, §15.2). Class N2. -/
217	theorem H05 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
218	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨101, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w .ub :=
219	  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
220	
221	/-- H05 twin: read of `[100, 104)`, ending at the end. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with the
222	written bytes (§15 ¶1, §16 ¶5). Class N2. -/
223	theorem H05_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
224	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨100, 0, 4, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 4 4)) :=
225	  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
226	
227	/-- Zero-length read access at address `104`, just after the end of `[96, 104)` (§15 ¶3). -/
228	def rz : Access := ⟨104, 0, 0, .read⟩
229	
230	/-- H06. Zero-length read just after the end of a dead allocation. Expected `ub`; obtained
231	`ub` (§15.1, §15 ¶3, §17 ¶3). Class N2. -/
232	theorem H06 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8d .ub :=
233	  ⟨run_a8d, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
234	
235	/-- H06 twin: same access, allocation live. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` with no bytes: the
236	spatial condition admits address `b + s` and no initialized byte is required (§15 ¶3).
237	Class N2. -/
238	theorem H06_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ReadStep ctxR rz () a8 (.ok []) :=
239	  ⟨run_a8, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
240	
241	/-! ## H07, H08 — creation preconditions -/
242	
243	/-- H07. Creation of `[100, 108)` in space `0`, overlapping the live `[96, 104)` of the same
244	space. Expected `ub`; obtained `ub` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
245	theorem H07 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8 .ub :=
246	  ⟨run_a8, allocStep_ub run_a8 (by decide)⟩
247	
248	/-- H07 twins: the same creation in another space (`1`), or in space `0` after the
249	overlapped allocation died. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
250	theorem H07_twin : AllocStep 1 100 8 4 none a8 (.ok (a8.alloc 1 100 8 4 none)) ∧
251	    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .dealloc 0 7] a8d ∧
252	    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none a8d (.ok (a8d.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
253	  ⟨allocStep_ok run_a8 (by decide), run_a8d, allocStep_ok run_a8d (by decide)⟩
254	
255	/-- H08. From the empty state (admissible, §9 ¶9): alignment `3`, not a power of two, with
256	base `96` a multiple of `3`; and base `100` not a multiple of alignment `8`. Expected `ub`;
257	obtained `ub` for both (§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
258	theorem H08 : AllocStep 0 96 8 3 none State.empty .ub ∧ AllocStep 0 100 8 8 none State.empty .ub :=
259	  ⟨allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ub run_empty (by decide)⟩
260	
261	/-- H08 twins: valid alignment `4` for each faulty creation. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok`
262	(§9 ¶4, §9 ¶11). Class N2. -/
263	theorem H08_twin :
264	    AllocStep 0 96 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 4 none)) ∧
265	    AllocStep 0 100 8 4 none State.empty (.ok (State.empty.alloc 0 100 8 4 none)) :=
266	  ⟨allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide), allocStep_ok run_empty (by decide)⟩
267	
268	/-! ## H09, H10 — write authority, derivation -/
269	
270	/-- H09. Write through an access whose elementary authority is `read`. Expected `ub`;
271	obtained `ub` (§12 ¶4, §16.3). Class N2. -/
272	theorem H09 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
273	    WriteStep ctxW ⟨96, 0, 8, .read⟩ () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
274	  ⟨run_a8, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩
275	
276	/-- H09 twin: write authority. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` (§16.3). Class N2. -/
277	theorem H09_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧
278	    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok a8w) :=
279	  ⟨run_a8, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩
280	
281	/-- Source access of H10: write access to `[96, 100)` of allocation `0` (§12 ¶1). -/
282	def h10src : Access := ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩
283	
284	/-- Access formed outside the source range `[96, 100)` but inside the allocation:
285	`[100, 104)` (§14 ¶4). -/
286	def h10out : Access := ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩
287	
288	/-- Access formed outside the source range and outside the allocation: `[104, 108)`
289	(§14 ¶4). -/
290	def h10past : Access := ⟨104, 0, 4, .write⟩
291	
292	/-- Restrictive derivation of `h10src` inside its range: `[98, 100)` (§14 ¶1). -/
293	def h10in : Access := ⟨98, 0, 2, .write⟩
294	
295	/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range that leaves the allocation.
296	Expected `ub` for the use; obtained `ub` (§15 ¶1, §16.2). The formation itself has no
297	transition in the machine and no verdict: open obligation (§14 ¶4, §19), not declared passed.
298	Class N2. -/
299	theorem H10 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10past ∧
300	    WriteStep ctxW h10past () Witness.w₀ a8 .ub :=
301	  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩
302	
303	/-- H10, use of an access formed outside the source range but inside the allocation.
304	Expected `ub`; obtained `ok`. Mismatch, case defect: provenance has allocation granularity in
305	the machine (§14 ¶2), so only leaving the allocation makes the use `ub` (§16.2); the scenario
306	does not say which. Class N2. -/
307	theorem H10_inside : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ ¬ Derive h10src h10out ∧
308	    WriteStep ctxW h10out () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10out Witness.w₀)) :=
309	  ⟨run_a8, fun h => absurd h.2.1 (by decide), .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩
310	
311	/-- H10 twin: a restrictive derivation inside the source range, then use. Expected `ok`;
312	obtained `ok` (§14 ¶1, §16). Class N2. -/
313	theorem H10_twin : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Derive h10src h10in ∧
314	    WriteStep ctxW h10in () Witness.w₀ a8 (.ok (a8.write h10in Witness.w₀)) :=
315	  ⟨run_a8, ⟨by decide, by decide, rfl, by decide⟩, .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩⟩
316	
317	/-! ## H11, H12 — read-after-write and non-interference -/
318	
319	/-- H11. Write `[96, 104)`, read the contained subrange `[98, 101)`. Expected: the written
320	sub-contents; obtained `ok` with positions `2..4` of the written representation (§16 ¶5).
321	Class N2. -/
322	theorem H11 : Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧
323	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨98, 0, 3, .read⟩ () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 2 3)) :=
324	  ⟨run_a8w, readStep_of (by decide)⟩
325	
326	/-- Second written representation of H12: byte `170`, no provenance, at every position
327	(§10 ¶2). -/
328	def w₁ : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => (170, none)
329	
330	/-- State of H12: allocations `0` (`[96, 104)`) and `1` (`[128, 136)`, same space), and
331	`[96, 100)` written with `Witness.w₀` (§9 ¶3, §16 ¶2). -/
332	abbrev h12 : State := (a8.alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ Witness.w₀
333	
334	/-- Operations reaching `h12` (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
335	abbrev h12Ops : List (Op Unit) :=
336	  [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .alloc 0 128 8 8 none, .write ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩ () Witness.w₀]
337	
338	/-- `h12` is reached (§9 ¶11, §16). -/
339	theorem run_h12 : Run h12Ops h12 :=
340	  run_write (run_alloc run_a8 (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial
341	
342	/-- H12. After `h12`, a write of a disjoint range of the same allocation (`[100, 104)`), or a
343	write of the other allocation, leaves the read of `[96, 100)` unchanged. Expected: contents
344	unchanged; obtained: the same `ok` bytes before and after each write (§16 ¶3, §16 ¶5).
345	Class N2. -/
346	theorem H12 : Run h12Ops h12 ∧
347	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () h12 (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
348	    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
349	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨100, 0, 4, .write⟩ w₁)
350	      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) ∧
351	    Run (h12Ops ++ [.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ () w₁]) (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁) ∧
352	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩ () (h12.write ⟨128, 1, 8, .write⟩ w₁)
353	      (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 4)) :=
354	  ⟨run_h12, readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
355	    readStep_of (by decide), run_write run_h12 (by decide) trivial trivial,
356	    readStep_of (by decide)⟩
357	
358	/-! ## H13a, H13b — pointer bytes -/
359	
360	/-- Representation written as a pointer: byte values of the address `64` (low byte first) and
361	provenance `0`, the allocation at `64`, on every byte. The byte encoding is a choice of this
362	test; the provenance comes from the written representation (§10 ¶4, §16 ¶2). -/
363	def ptrRep : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun i => (if i = 0 then 64 else 0, some 0)
364	
365	/-- State of H13a before the copy: allocations `0` (`[64, 72)`), `1` (`[96, 104)`, source)
366	and `2` (`[128, 136)`, destination); `ptrRep` written over the source (§9 ¶11, §16 ¶2). -/
367	abbrev h13Src : State :=
368	  (((State.empty.alloc 0 64 8 8 none).alloc 0 96 8 8 none).alloc 0 128 8 8 none).write
369	    ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ ptrRep
370	
371	/-- Read access to source byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
372	def srcByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨96 + k, 1, 1, .read⟩
373	
374	/-- Write access to destination byte `k` (§12 ¶1). -/
375	def dstByte (k : Nat) : Access := ⟨128 + k, 2, 1, .write⟩
376	
377	/-- Representation supplied by the copy of byte `k`: the value and provenance of source byte
378	`k` (§16 ¶2). `cp_reads` shows that it is the abstract byte the copy read (§20.2 ¶1). -/
379	def copyRep (k : Nat) : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun _ => ptrRep k
380	
381	/-- State after copying the first `k` bytes, one byte per write (§16 ¶2). -/
382	def cp : Nat → State
383	  | 0 => h13Src
384	  | k + 1 => (cp k).write (dstByte k) (copyRep k)
385	
386	/-- Operations reaching `cp k`: set-up, then for each byte a read of the source byte and a
387	write of the destination byte (§15, §16). -/
388	def cpOps : Nat → List (Op Unit)
389	  | 0 => [.alloc 0 64 8 8 none, .alloc 0 96 8 8 none, .alloc 0 128 8 8 none,
390	      .write ⟨96, 1, 8, .write⟩ () ptrRep]
391	  | k + 1 => cpOps k ++ [.read (srcByte k) ()] ++ [.write (dstByte k) () (copyRep k)]
392	
393	/-- Before copying byte `k`, the read of source byte `k` is `ok` and returns exactly the value
394	and provenance that `copyRep k` supplies (§15, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). -/
395	theorem cp_reads : ∀ k, k < 8 →
396	    read Witness.obR (srcByte k) () (cp k) trivial = .ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2] := by
397	  decide
398	
399	/-- Before copying byte `k`, the write of destination byte `k` satisfies the kernel write
400	conditions (§16.1–§16.3). -/
401	theorem cp_writes : ∀ k, k < 8 → CanWrite (cp k) (dstByte k) := by
402	  decide
403	
404	/-- The copy of the first `k ≤ 8` bytes is an execution of `ok` steps from the empty state
405	(§20.3 ¶3). -/
406	theorem run_cp : ∀ k, k ≤ 8 → Run (cpOps k) (cp k)
407	  | 0, _ =>
408	    run_write (run_alloc (run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)) (by decide))
409	      (by decide) trivial trivial
410	  | k + 1, hk =>
411	    run_write (run_read (run_cp k (Nat.le_of_succ_le hk)) (read_sound (cp_reads k hk)))
412	      (cp_writes k hk) trivial trivial
413	
414	/-- The eight abstract bytes of `ptrRep`, each with provenance `0` (§10 ¶2). -/
415	def ptrBytes : List AByte :=
416	  [.init 64 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0),
417	    .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0), .init 0 (some 0)]
418	
419	/-- H13a. Pointer bytes copied byte by byte, each write supplying the abstract byte just read.
420	Expected: the provenance of each byte is kept. Obtained, at relation level: every copy read is
421	`ok` with the byte's value and provenance, and after the copy the destination reads exactly
422	the source bytes, provenance `0` on each (§16 ¶2, §16 ¶5, §20.2 ¶1). Open obligation, not
423	declared passed: whether a byte copy of the language supplies the read provenance is not fixed
424	(§10 ¶4, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
425	theorem H13a : Run (cpOps 8) (cp 8) ∧
426	    (∀ k, k < 8 → ReadStep ctxR (srcByte k) () (cp k) (.ok [.init (ptrRep k).1 (ptrRep k).2])) ∧
427	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨128, 2, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) ∧
428	    ReadStep ctxR ⟨96, 1, 8, .read⟩ () (cp 8) (.ok ptrBytes) :=
429	  ⟨run_cp 8 (Nat.le_refl _), fun k hk => read_sound (cp_reads k hk),
430	    readStep_of (by decide +kernel), readStep_of (by decide +kernel)⟩
431	
432	/-- H13b. Rebuilding a usable access from the copied bytes or from the integer `64`.
433	Expected: to be arbitrated. Obtained: no verdict; the machine has no conversion from an integer
434	or from bytes to an access, and an access to address `64` gets `ok` or `ub` according to the
435	provenance a conversion rule would give it: `0` (the provenance stored in the copied bytes)
436	gives `ok`, `2` (the allocation holding the copied bytes) gives `ub`. Open obligation, not
437	declared passed (§19.2, §19.3, §19 ¶3). Class N2. -/
438	theorem H13b_open :
439	    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) (.ok ((cp 8).write ⟨64, 0, 1, .write⟩ w₁)) ∧
440	    WriteStep ctxW ⟨64, 2, 1, .write⟩ () w₁ (cp 8) .ub :=
441	  ⟨.ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩, .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide)⟩
442	
443	/-! ## H14 — false static obligation -/
444	
445	/-- Read obligations whose decidable part is `True` and whose static part is `P` at every read
446	(§20.3 ¶1, §20.3 ¶2): an explicit context with a false (`P = False`) or true (`P = True`)
447	static obligation. -/
448	def obStat (P : Prop) : ReadObl Unit :=
449	  { dec := fun _ _ _ => True, stat := fun _ _ _ => P, decInst := fun _ _ _ => instDecidableTrue }
450	
451	/-- H14. Read of initialized bytes satisfying every kernel condition, under a context whose
452	static obligation is false. Expected: relation `ub`, interpreter not callable. Obtained: the
453	relation is `ub` (§20.1 ¶2, "including when the obligation is static"), and no proof of the
454	static part exists, so `read (obStat False) (rd 0) () a8w` cannot be applied (§20.3 ¶3).
455	Class N2. -/
456	theorem H14 :
457	    Exec (· = ·) (obStat False).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
458	      State.empty a8w ∧
459	    CanRead a8w (rd 0) ∧ ReadStep (obStat False).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w .ub ∧
460	    ¬ (obStat False).stat a8w (rd 0) () :=
461	  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, by decide,
462	    .ub fun h => h.2.2, id⟩
463	
464	/-- H14 twin: same access, static obligation true. Expected `ok`; obtained `ok` by the
465	relation and by the interpreter, with the same bytes (§20.1 ¶2, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
466	theorem H14_twin :
467	    Exec (· = ·) (obStat True).toSpec ctxW [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀]
468	      State.empty a8w ∧
469	    ReadStep (obStat True).toSpec (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
470	    read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) :=
471	  have hr : read (obStat True) (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) := by
472	    decide
473	  ⟨run_write (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide) trivial trivial, read_sound hr, hr⟩
474	
475	/-! ## H15, H16 — zero-size allocations, deallocation with a live access -/
476	
477	/-- State of H15: two allocations of size `0` at base `96` in space `0` (§9 ¶3). -/
478	abbrev h15 : State := (State.empty.alloc 0 96 0 8 none).alloc 0 96 0 8 none
479	
480	/-- H15. Two zero-size allocations live at the same base. Expected `ok`, distinct identities;
481	obtained: both creations `ok`, the state is admissible, identities `0` and `1` are both live
482	at base `96` with size `0` (§9 ¶3, §9 ¶8, §13 ¶1). Class N2. -/
483	theorem H15 : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 ∧ Admissible h15 ∧
484	    (∃ a, h15.allocs 0 = some a ∧ a.live = true ∧ a.base = 96 ∧ a.size = 0) ∧
485	    (∃ b, h15.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96 ∧ b.size = 0) :=
486	  have hr : Run [.alloc 0 96 0 8 none, .alloc 0 96 0 8 none] h15 :=
487	    run_alloc (run_alloc (.nil _) (by decide)) (by decide)
488	  ⟨hr, hr.admissible admissible_empty, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩⟩
489	
490	/-- State of H16: `a8w` (written through `wr 0`), then deallocation of `0` (§17 ¶3). -/
491	abbrev h16 : State := a8w.dealloc 0
492	
493	/-- H16. Deallocation while the access `wr 0` designates the allocation, then use of that
494	access. Expected `ok`, then `ub`; obtained: the deallocation is `ok` (its conditions do not
495	mention existing accesses, §17.1, §17.2), then the write and the read through provenance `0`
496	are `ub` (§15.1, §16.1, §17 ¶3). Prevention belongs to the access discipline. Class N2. -/
497	theorem H16 :
498	    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀, .dealloc 0 7] h16 ∧
499	    DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 a8w (.ok h16) ∧
500	    WriteStep ctxW (wr 0) () Witness.w₀ h16 .ub ∧ ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () h16 .ub :=
501	  ⟨run_dealloc run_a8w (by decide), .ok (by decide), .ub fun h => absurd h.1 (by decide),
502	    readStep_of (by decide)⟩
503	
504	/-! ## H17 — relation and interpreter -/
505	
506	/-- On a state, every outcome of the read relation is the interpreter's result and conversely
507	(§20.3 ¶3, `read_sound`, `read_complete`). -/
508	theorem read_agree (ac : Access) (s : State) (o : ReadOutcome) :
509	    ReadStep ctxR ac () s o ↔ read Witness.obR ac () s trivial = o :=
510	  ⟨fun h => read_complete h trivial, read_sound⟩
511	
512	/-- H17. Read by the relation and by the interpreter on admissible reached states. Expected:
513	same outcome, same value. Obtained: on `a8w` both give `ok` with the written bytes, on `a8`
514	both give `ub`, and the outcome sets coincide (§9 ¶8, §20.1, §20.2 ¶1, §20.3 ¶3). Class N2. -/
515	theorem H17 :
516	    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write (wr 0) () Witness.w₀] a8w ∧ Admissible a8w ∧
517	    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = o) ∧
518	    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8w (.ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8)) ∧
519	    read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8w trivial = .ok (writtenBytes Witness.w₀ 0 8) ∧
520	    Run [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)] a8 ∧ Admissible a8 ∧
521	    (∀ o, ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 o ↔ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = o) ∧
522	    ReadStep ctxR (rd 0) () a8 .ub ∧ read Witness.obR (rd 0) () a8 trivial = .ub :=
523	  ⟨run_a8w, run_a8w.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04_twin.2, by decide,
524	    run_a8, run_a8.admissible admissible_empty, read_agree _ _, H04.2, by decide⟩
525	
526	end Ern.Corpus.MM2H

1	# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique
2	
3	**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
4	**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
5	**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).
6	
7	## 0. Règles du jalon 3
8	
9	1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
10	2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
11	3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
12	4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
13	5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
14	6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
15	7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
16	8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

184	## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)
185	
186	**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. Aucun drapeau d'emprunt par entrée : l'exclusivité d'une résolution `Modify` découle des règles du noyau (I1, O3.2), par la forme de l'arbre de dérivation ci-dessous.
187	
188	**État de l'entrée de pool** (abstrait, comme l'entrée d'arène ; sa représentation en octets est une obligation de l'implémentation) : `{id, storage, internal, slots}`.
189	- `id` : identité de pool fraîche à chaque `newPool`, jamais réutilisée pendant l'exécution. Un pool détruit puis recréé, même sur le même stockage, a une autre identité.
190	- `slots` : chaque entrée est `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}` ; `place` est une partie de `storage`.
191	- La valeur pool est le détenteur de `internal` (même règle que F1). Le stockage peut être local, statique, alloué ou un bloc.
192	
193	**Handle** : `(id, slot, gen)`, une donnée de taille fixe.
194	
195	**Emprunt composé.** Une résolution est un emprunt composé : une autorité **compagne** dérivée de `internal` sur **tout le stockage** du pool, au mode de la résolution, détenue par le cadre courant ; puis une autorité d'**entrée** par handle résolu, dérivée **de la compagne** (sous-empreinte), au même mode, détenue par le cadre courant et étiquetée de la génération résolue. Conséquences, toutes par les règles existantes du noyau :
196	- la compagne ne peut être libérée tant qu'une de ses autorités d'entrée est active (O3.2) ;
197	- une compagne `Modify` active rend le mode effectif de `internal` absent sur tout le stockage : toute nouvelle résolution, `Modify` ou `Observe`, est rejetée, quels que soient les handles ;
198	- plusieurs compagnes `Observe` coexistent ; une résolution `Modify` est alors rejetée.
199	
200	**Opérations**
201	
202	- **`newPool storage internal`** : préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2, J1) ; identité fraîche ; toutes les entrées libres, générations à 0.
203	- **`allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool (`Modify` exerçable ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`) ; `dst` est une feuille non `Init`, ne détenant aucune autorité active, de la taille d'un handle, `Modify` exerçable ; `fail` si aucune entrée libre (état inchangé) ; `ok` : une entrée libre devient vivante, son contenu reste `Uninit`, le handle `(id, slot, gen)` est écrit dans `dst`, qui seule passe à `Init`.
204	- **`resolve h m : ok | fail | reject`** (`m` = `Observe` ou `Modify`) : droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` par la valeur pool ; les vérifications d'identité et de génération lisent seulement les métadonnées et précèdent toute création d'autorité ; `fail` (état inchangé) si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée, ou si l'entrée est libre ; `ok` : emprunt composé à une entrée. Une compagne déjà active n'est jamais réutilisée : chaque résolution crée la sienne.
205	- **`resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject`** : une compagne, une autorité d'entrée par handle (par `split` de la compagne) ; `fail` si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool, ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée ; **atomique** : en cas de `fail`, aucune autorité n'est créée. Coût dynamique explicite : vérification de distinction proportionnelle au lot. C'est la voie des requêtes ECS.
206	- **`unresolve`** : `release` des autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne.
207	- **`freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool ; `fail` si `h` est périmé ou d'un autre pool ; `reject` si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre l'entrée (donc pendant toute résolution du pool, puisque chaque compagne couvre tout le stockage) ; sinon fin logique du contenu de l'entrée **selon `endUse`** (mêmes préconditions : aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ; mêmes effets : feuilles `Uninit`, autorités détenues libérées, dépendances supprimées, stockage possédé logiquement mort, sans désallocation) — `reject` si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue ; une entrée déjà `Uninit` est acceptée ; puis l'entrée devient libre et sa génération est incrémentée.
208	
209	**Invariant `PoolInv`** (tout pool vivant) : entrées deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; toute autorité active dérivée d'une compagne du pool sur une entrée porte la génération courante de l'entrée, et l'entrée est vivante ; toute compagne active a au plus les autorités d'entrée de sa résolution pour descendants.
210	
211	**Générations et identités** : `Nat` dans le modèle ; le débordement des générations et l'unicité réelle des identités de pool sont des obligations de l'implémentation, classées bibliothèque et spec 11.
212	
213	**Théorèmes attendus**
214	- `pool_resolve_stale_fails`, `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` ;
215	- `pool_no_stale_access` : aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ;
216	- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` : sur tout état atteint, au plus une compagne `Modify` active par pool, et alors aucune compagne `Observe` — quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve` qui y mène ;
217	- `pool_resolveMany_atomic` et `pool_resolveMany_distinct` ;
218	- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` : après `freeSlot`, le contenu de l'entrée satisfait les effets d'`endUse` ;

223	## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage
224	
225	**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.
226	
227	**Options**
228	
229	1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
230	2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
231	3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.
232	
233	**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
234	- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
235	- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
236	- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?
237	
238	**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

181	
182	---
183	
184	## 4. Contrat du pool de handles (instance de bibliothèque, comme l'arène)
185	
186	**Principe.** Un handle est une donnée ; il ne porte aucune autorité. La résolution fournit un accès temporaire de seconde classe. Aucun drapeau d'emprunt par entrée : l'exclusivité d'une résolution `Modify` découle des règles du noyau (I1, O3.2), par la forme de l'arbre de dérivation ci-dessous.
187	
188	**État de l'entrée de pool** (abstrait, comme l'entrée d'arène ; sa représentation en octets est une obligation de l'implémentation) : `{id, storage, internal, slots}`.
189	- `id` : identité de pool fraîche à chaque `newPool`, jamais réutilisée pendant l'exécution. Un pool détruit puis recréé, même sur le même stockage, a une autre identité.
190	- `slots` : chaque entrée est `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}` ; `place` est une partie de `storage`.
191	- La valeur pool est le détenteur de `internal` (même règle que F1). Le stockage peut être local, statique, alloué ou un bloc.
192	
193	**Handle** : `(id, slot, gen)`, une donnée de taille fixe.
194	
195	**Emprunt composé.** Une résolution est un emprunt composé : une autorité **compagne** dérivée de `internal` sur **tout le stockage** du pool, au mode de la résolution, détenue par le cadre courant ; puis une autorité d'**entrée** par handle résolu, dérivée **de la compagne** (sous-empreinte), au même mode, détenue par le cadre courant et étiquetée de la génération résolue. Conséquences, toutes par les règles existantes du noyau :
196	- la compagne ne peut être libérée tant qu'une de ses autorités d'entrée est active (O3.2) ;
197	- une compagne `Modify` active rend le mode effectif de `internal` absent sur tout le stockage : toute nouvelle résolution, `Modify` ou `Observe`, est rejetée, quels que soient les handles ;
198	- plusieurs compagnes `Observe` coexistent ; une résolution `Modify` est alors rejetée.
199	
200	**Opérations**
201	
202	- **`newPool storage internal`** : préconditions de `newArena` (F1, F2, J1) ; identité fraîche ; toutes les entrées libres, générations à 0.
203	- **`allocSlot pool dst : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool (`Modify` exerçable ou `writeShared` sur métadonnées `SharedMutable`) ; `dst` est une feuille non `Init`, ne détenant aucune autorité active, de la taille d'un handle, `Modify` exerçable ; `fail` si aucune entrée libre (état inchangé) ; `ok` : une entrée libre devient vivante, son contenu reste `Uninit`, le handle `(id, slot, gen)` est écrit dans `dst`, qui seule passe à `Init`.
204	- **`resolve h m : ok | fail | reject`** (`m` = `Observe` ou `Modify`) : droit d'exercice de `internal` au mode `m` par la valeur pool ; les vérifications d'identité et de génération lisent seulement les métadonnées et précèdent toute création d'autorité ; `fail` (état inchangé) si `h.id` n'est pas l'identité du pool, si `h.gen` diffère de la génération de l'entrée, ou si l'entrée est libre ; `ok` : emprunt composé à une entrée. Une compagne déjà active n'est jamais réutilisée : chaque résolution crée la sienne.
205	- **`resolveMany hs m : ok | fail | reject`** : une compagne, une autorité d'entrée par handle (par `split` de la compagne) ; `fail` si un handle est périmé ou d'un autre pool, ou si deux handles désignent la même entrée ; **atomique** : en cas de `fail`, aucune autorité n'est créée. Coût dynamique explicite : vérification de distinction proportionnelle au lot. C'est la voie des requêtes ECS.
206	- **`unresolve`** : `release` des autorités d'entrée, puis de la compagne.
207	- **`freeSlot h : ok | fail | reject`** : droit de mise à jour sur la valeur pool ; `fail` si `h` est périmé ou d'un autre pool ; `reject` si une autorité active dérivée de `internal` couvre l'entrée (donc pendant toute résolution du pool, puisque chaque compagne couvre tout le stockage) ; sinon fin logique du contenu de l'entrée **selon `endUse`** (mêmes préconditions : aucune dépendance utilisable, aucune feuille épinglée ; mêmes effets : feuilles `Uninit`, autorités détenues libérées, dépendances supprimées, stockage possédé logiquement mort, sans désallocation) — `reject` si une précondition d'`endUse` échoue ; une entrée déjà `Uninit` est acceptée ; puis l'entrée devient libre et sa génération est incrémentée.
208	
209	**Invariant `PoolInv`** (tout pool vivant) : entrées deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; toute autorité active dérivée d'une compagne du pool sur une entrée porte la génération courante de l'entrée, et l'entrée est vivante ; toute compagne active a au plus les autorités d'entrée de sa résolution pour descendants.
210	
211	**Générations et identités** : `Nat` dans le modèle ; le débordement des générations et l'unicité réelle des identités de pool sont des obligations de l'implémentation, classées bibliothèque et spec 11.
212	
213	**Théorèmes attendus**
214	- `pool_resolve_stale_fails`, `pool_resolve_other_pool_fails` ;
215	- `pool_no_stale_access` : aucune autorité active d'une génération périmée ;
216	- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive` : sur tout état atteint, au plus une compagne `Modify` active par pool, et alors aucune compagne `Observe` — quelle que soit la séquence de `resolve`, `resolveMany`, `release`, `store`, `transfer` et `unresolve` qui y mène ;
217	- `pool_resolveMany_atomic` et `pool_resolveMany_distinct` ;
218	- `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` : après `freeSlot`, le contenu de l'entrée satisfait les effets d'`endUse` ;
219	- `pool_inv_preserved`, et intégration à `Reachable` dans un module séparé, noyau inchangé.
220	
221	**Cas** : H30–H34b, H44, W1.
222	
223	## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage
224	
225	**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.
226	
227	**Options**
228	
229	1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
230	2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
231	3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.
232	
233	**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
234	- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
235	- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
236	- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?
237	
238	**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.
239	
240	---
241	
242	## 5b. Scénarios d'usage (exigences de validation, pas une description de l'implémentation actuelle de Weld)
243	
244	| ID | Structure | Séquence | Attendu |
245	|---|---|---|---|
246	| W1 | Graphe de scène | Pool de nœuds `{data, parent : handle, child : handle}` sur une allocation ; deux nœuds liés dans les deux sens par handles ; `resolve` `Modify` d'un nœud, écriture de `data`, `unresolve` ; `freeSlot` d'un nœud encore désigné par le handle de l'autre ; `resolve` de ce handle ; `freeSlot` pendant une résolution active | tout `ok` ; `resolve` du handle périmé : `fail` ; `freeSlot` pendant résolution : `reject` |
247	| W2 | ECS archetype + sparse set | Archetype à deux colonnes (SoA) sur une allocation ; `split` des colonnes ; système A écrit la colonne 1 pendant que le système B lit la colonne 2 ; `resolveMany` `Modify` de trois entités distinctes d'un pool d'entités ; déplacement d'une entité vers un autre archetype (transferts des champs de la ligne) pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération | lectures et écritures disjointes `ok` ; `resolveMany` `ok` ; déplacement pendant la vue : `reject` ; après : `ok` |
248	| W3 | Arène de frame | `alloc`, `newArena`, trois `issue`, trois vues rangées (`store`) dans une structure locale ; `reset` pendant que les vues vivent ; `endUse` de la structure ; `reset` ; réémission | `reset` pendant : `reject` ; après : `ok` ; réémission `ok` |
249	
250	## 6. Registre des obligations inter-spécifications
251	
252	| Obligation | Destination |
253	|---|---|
254	| `stat` (composante concurrente des obligations opaques) ; transférabilité, partageabilité ; H39, H41 | spec 2 |
255	| Protection forte des paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; H27b ; H38, H40, H42 ; `defer` | spec 3 |
256	| `dec` (validité de représentation) ; `SameSizeAlong` ; une référence se range dans un emplacement de type référence ; `kind` comme point d'accroche ; le type d'un pointeur porte la forme d'une région non contiguë (le pointeur n'en désigne que l'adresse la plus basse) | spec 4 |
257	| `dec` (alignement des accès) ; taille d'un pointeur et encodage `decode` ; largeur des adresses et épuisement de l'espace ; débordement des générations ; placement (`PlacementOK`), jetons (`TokCompat`) | spec 11 |
258	| Traduction bas niveau de `noalias` | spec 13 |
259	| Obligation de libération attachée à certains types ; H43 | spécification des ressources |
260	| `DeclaredDisjoint` (disjonction des feuilles déclarées) ; `FreeCompat` ; représentation des métadonnées d'arène et de pool | bibliothèque |
261	
262	## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence
263	
264	0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.
265	1. Écarts du brouillon MM-03 trouvés au jalon 2 (passe 1, (f) 1–6) : utilisabilité des feuilles lues et écrites ; empreintes faites de feuilles ; une racine par `alloc` ; marques de mort transitives ; `RootLive` ; bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
266	2. Locaux d'`enterFrame` possédés directement par le cadre (O6, à écrire dans la v0.3).
267	3. Décisions 1 à 4 du jalon 2 : disjonction déclarée par feuilles ; pointeur d'une région vide ; adresse la plus basse ; feuille de référence de la taille d'un pointeur.
268	4. Théorèmes à énoncer : induction « toute feuille `Init` atteinte a été déclarée ou écrite » ; correspondance `Step` ↔ `Reachable`.
269	5. Noms Lean des textes normatifs déplacés en annexe de correspondance.
270

1	# Task brief (verbatim obligations, as given by the user)
2	
3	Normative hierarchy: Charter v0 highest (contradictions reported, never resolved); spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md validated and frozen, cite by section; draft branches formal/* are material only (reuse when matching the spec, divergences resolved in favor of the spec and listed).
4	Layout (suggested): Ern/MemoryModel/Machine.lean (Part III), Ern/MemoryModel/Access/*.lean (Parts IV-XIII, XV-XVI), Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean (Part XIV: arenas as reference library abstraction; O17-O19 derived over O1-O16 plus metadata; ArenaInv and the §56 guard as abstraction contract), Ern/MemoryModel/Refinement.lean (§82), Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean, Ern/Lib/DataStack.lean (non-normative), test modules imported by no model module. MM-01 (Part II) referenced, not a module.
5	
6	Obligations (all mandatory):
7	1. Machine (Part III). Relations total and deterministic; interpreters calculable with static obligations and WF as proof arguments; agreement theorems both ways on their domain; admissible-state invariants preserved; P1-P4, no double free, frame lemmas, read-after-write on every included sub-range (§16).
8	2. Kernel (Parts IV-XIII). Every operation exactly as written, including §63.8 and §77 local self-blocking prevention, §65 store rules (derived authority, free leaf, arrival-state exercisability), §72 parameter-origin rule, §73 reanchoring to the first surviving active origin, §69/§70 end of use and free, pinning rules. Locals created by entering a frame are owned directly by the frame; alloc creates exactly one root. Theorems: preservation of WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan by every step; reachable invariant from S3.init statics under DDSound; exitFrame_no_dangling; call_params_effective_protected; effective_exclusive; init_only_by_writes, init_statics, and the global induction (every Init leaf of a reached state was declared or written); correspondence between Step and Reachable.
9	3. Arena (Part XIV). issue_as_kernel, reset_as_kernel (both directions, same arrival state on the kernel part), newArena_as_library (no safety property depends on the guard), arena_reuse_safe, ArenaInv preserved.
10	4. Refinement (§82). Repr including MM-02 WF; R1, R2, R4, R6 for every kernel operation and derived arena operation; simulation with parameters fixed once per run; freeSound_derived; pinned_address_stable; exclusive_bytes. Decisions to apply: declared disjointness is disjointness of leaves (byte disjointness follows from layout well-formedness); a pointer to an empty region has address = base of the effective anchor's allocation and that allocation as provenance; a region's pointer address is the lowest address among its non-empty leaves; a leaf receiving a reference has pointer size (stated hypothesis, classed types/ABI).
11	5. HandlePool (contract: v0.4 annex). Composite borrow (companion derived from internal over the whole storage, entries derived from the companion); resolveMany Observe by Observe derivations, distinctness only in Modify; allocSlot/freeSlot require a live pool and Modify on the pool value; newPool requires Uninit storage; freeSlot ends the entry content with endUse effects, preconditions excluding internal and its ancestors; PoolInv = entry disjointness + pool_no_stale_access + transition guarantee that freeSlot never succeeds on an entry covered by an active companion descendant. Theorems: pool_resolve_modify_exclusive, pool_no_stale_access, stale/other-pool/atomicity/distinctness, pool_freeSlot_ends_content under the Modify right.
12	6. DataStack (contract below, identifier DS-v1). Marks carry stack identity and a fresh mark identifier; the stack keeps the ordered list of live marks; rewind m fails on a dead or foreign mark, rejects if an active authority derived from internal covers a cell above m, otherwise returns those cells to available and removes m and every mark above it; push and grow use the derived issue; grow is in place only (same base, extension into the space directly after the block, fail otherwise). Theorems: rewind_rejects_live_above, mark_no_aba (for every removed mark), rewind_keeps_older_marks, grow_same_base, grow_keeps_prefix_init, grow_keeps_prefix_bytes through the refinement.
13	7. Corpora. Encode MM2-H (first execution), MM3-H and MM23-H (replay) from the attached material, plus new cases: §63.8 and §77 self-blocking (reject, with twins), §56 guard, corrected HandlePool, DataStack (including ABA and a multi-stack frame scenario), W1-W3. Each case: reached state from the initial state, expected verdict from its source, positive twin for each rejection, class. MM23-H15 and H16 must now pass. Section J of MM3-H stays unencoded and classified. No case is corrected or bypassed.
14	
15	Docstrings: model modules: every def/theorem cites the specification clause it formalizes. Library modules: cite the applicable spec clauses (§36, §56, ...) and the local contract identifier (HandlePool v0.4 annex, DS-v1), stated as non-normative.
16	Exclusions: instrumented checked variants; duplicate _pre statements; references to draft reports; concurrency beyond the stat boundary; syntax.
17	Rules: zero sorry; #print axioms at most {propext, Quot.sound} on every constant (checked by script); no noncomputable; lake build without warnings; nothing invented - a clause that cannot be formalized as written is reported, not interpreted; no statement weakened relative to its clause; adversarial review rounds, every finding re-checked by a refuter.
18	Opening the PR: only if every mandatory obligation is proved and every expected/obtained mismatch resolved; otherwise commit on the branch, do not push, do not open the PR, end with a blocking report (each unproved obligation or mismatch classified as specification defect, module defect or case defect, with its counterexample). Never present a partial formalization as conforming.

import Ern.Corpus.Runner

/-!
# Corpus MM3-H: access discipline, sections A–F, H, I (test module)

The cases of corpus MM3-H of the Jalon 3 material (`ERN_Jalon3_materiel.md`, §1; non-normative
design material), run on the reference kernel and arena of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` (§60–§78), plus new cases fixed by spec clauses and the
usage scenario W3 (material §5b). This is a test module: no model module imports it.

Each case is a run from `LState.init statics` (§47) by the runner (`Ern.Corpus.Runner`):
`RunsTo k statics os L` states that every step is `ok` and that `L` is library-reachable and its
kernel state `Reachable` (§57). The verdict of the step under test is stated with the relation of
its operation (`DeriveStep`, `TransferStep`, `IssueD`, `ResetD`, …) on the reached state and
decided by `decide`. Each docstring gives the expected verdict from the case's source (the
material, or the spec clause for new cases), the obtained verdict, the class (material §0, rule 5:
`N3` kernel, `Lib` library instance, `spec 3` another specification) and the positive twin (rule 2:
the same sequence without the faulty element, accepted). A case whose obtained verdict differs from
the expected one is kept with its expected verdict and marked **MISMATCH** with its cause; no case
is corrected.

Twins that are not literally the same sequence without one faulty step:
* another destination, target, parameter or identity in place of the faulty one: H04 (the other
  element), H13 (`z`), H18 (the local leaf 3), H21 (a `Modify` parameter), H25 (a `Modify`
  parameter on the static), H29 (a `Modify` parameter), H50 `transfer` (the stored authority on
  the local 4), H50 `issue` (the value 2), H51 direct form (the view on `u`), S63_8 (the stored
  authority on the local 6), S56 (`internal` 5), S77_2 (the destination 3 outside the region,
  `fail`; the available region `[6]`, `ok`);
* further steps that lift the blocking before the step under test: H11 (`endUse` of `v2` and of
  the leaf 6), H17 (`endUse` of the block value, then `free` of the storage 4 instead of the leaf
  5), H19 (`endUse` of the child value), H26 second twin (the contract with `ExternalDone`, then
  `unpin`), H27b (three `release`), W3 (`endUse` of the structure and of the block values);
* a pairing given by the material: H05 (its own twin), H21b (H37);
* a faulty element of several steps, removed: H03, S77_6 (`derive` and `store`), H51 through a
  helper (the view, or its `store`), H49 (the six steps of the cycle: removing only its stores
  leaves the `reject`, for another cause);
* no twin: the `reset` `reject` in the state `h49` of H49, which persists without the cycle
  (construction defect by rule 2, recorded there); the reception `transfer` `reject` of H16, a
  **MISMATCH** whose expected verdict is `ok`.

Local shapes are lists of (parent, kind) (§72, §71.1); `lf` is a root leaf, `pt p` a part of `p`.
Place and authority identities are list indices (§38): `enterFrame` appends the locals and one
root authority per root local; `alloc` appends the shape and one root authority; `derive` and
`split` append the derived authorities; `issue` appends one block authority; `reset` appends one
(released) authority.

Not encoded here:
* section G (H30–H34b, H44, handle pools) and the usage scenarios W1, W2 (they use a handle pool):
  later wave (`HandlePool`);
* the cross-registry cases of §56 (a pool and an arena, or two pools, on one `internal`): later
  wave; only the arena registry exists here (`S56`);
* section J, out of the kernel, classified by the material: H38 get-or-insert cache (spec 3,
  flow-sensitive liveness, §25, §32); H39 suspended coroutine holding a `Modify` parameter
  (specs 2 and 3, §29, §81); H40 raw pointer used during a call (spec 3 and the boundary of §19,
  §81); H41 concurrent `writeShared` (spec 2, §18, §24, §68); H42 `defer free(x)` then
  `transfer(x)` (spec 3, `defer` is outside the kernel, §73, §81); H43 resource with a release
  obligation (resource specification, §7).
-/

namespace Ern.Corpus.MM3H

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access Ern.MemoryModel.Arena Ern.Corpus

/-! ## Test contracts and shapes (§48, §72) -/

/-- The empty test contract (§48): nothing shared, pinned, externally done or deallocable. -/
abbrev K0 : K := KD.toK {}

/-- A root leaf of a local shape (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev lf : Option Nat × Nat := (none, 0)

/-- A leaf part of the shape element `p` (§72, §71.1). -/
abbrev pt (p : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat := (some p, 0)

/-- A structure 0 with the parts 1 and 2 (§40, §72). -/
def S2 : LocalShape := [lf, pt 0, pt 0]

/-- A write of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§67.1: the writing authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem write_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Write3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Write3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- A read of `ls` rejected for every authority of the state is rejected for every authority
(§66.2: the reading authority is exercisable, hence exists, §43). -/
theorem read_rejected {s : S3} {ls : List Nat}
    (h : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ Read3Pre s a ls) (a : Nat) :
    Read3Step a ls s .reject :=
  .reject fun hp => h a (List.mem_range.2 (exercisable_lt hp.exercisable)) hp

/-- The preconditions of `transfer` other than local self-blocking prevention (§63.1–§63.7), the
fields of `TransferPre` but `noSelfLock`: used to show that §63.8 alone rejects a transfer. -/
def TransferPreBut638 (k : K) (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable src ∧ s.Usable dst ∧ HasRight s .modify src ∧ HasRight s .modify dst ∧
    SameShape s.P src dst ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, s.I l = .init) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P dst, s.I l ≠ .init) ∧ ¬ overlap s.P src dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, ¬ ActiveDerivedOutside s src j) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ footprint s.P src, ¬ k.Pinned l ∧ s.pin l = false) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ movedDeps s src, s.Active x) ∧ AnchorOrder (transferEff s src dst) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, AnchorMoves s src x →
      ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (transferEff s src dst).Usable q →
        OptP ((transferEff s src dst).A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
          EffAnchorOK (transferEff s src dst) x ((transferEff s src dst).pframe q)) True)

/-- Decidability of `TransferPreBut638` (§63). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (src dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (TransferPreBut638 k s src dst) := by
  unfold TransferPreBut638; infer_instance

/-- The static preconditions of `issue` other than local self-blocking prevention (§77.1, §77.2),
the fields of `IssueStatic` but `dstNotIn`: used to show that this clause alone rejects. -/
def IssueStaticBut (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Active E.internal ∧ MetaRight s E ∧ (∀ l ∈ region, l ∈ footprint s.P E.storage) ∧
    s.Usable dst ∧ isLeaf s.P dst ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length,
      OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun z => z.active = true → z.holder ≠ .place dst) True) ∧
    HasRight s .modify dst

/-- Decidability of `IssueStaticBut` (§77). -/
instance (s : S3) (E : ArenaEntry) (region : List Nat) (dst : Nat) :
    Decidable (IssueStaticBut s E region dst) := by
  unfold IssueStaticBut; infer_instance

/-- Run of H01 (§72, §60): frame 1 with structure 0 (parts 1, 2, root authority 0);
`derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` gives the first parameter, authority 1. -/
def h01o : List Op := [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 [1, 2] .modify]

/-- **H01** (material §1 A, class N3). Two parameters derived from one local, `Modify` on the
whole, then `Observe` on a part. Expected (material): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: the root has no
effective mode on the part, covered by the active `Modify` descendant 1 (§43 case 3), so the
`Observe` derivation exceeds it (§60.2). Twin without the first parameter: the `derive` is `ok`;
and the call with the first parameter alone is `ok` (§72). -/
theorem H01 : RunsTo K0 [] h01o h01 ∧ DeriveStep 0 [1] .observe h01.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] S2, .derive 0 [1] .observe] ∧ Runs K0 [] (h01o ++ [.enter [1] []]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

authority 7, so that only the structural clause can reject. -/
abbrev KF45 : K := KD.toK { dealloc := [4, 5], compat := [(4, 7), (5, 7)] }

/-- Run of H17, H18 (§72, §71, §76, §77): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator 1, values 2 and 3;
storage 4 (leaves 5, 6) owned by 0; arena on 4 with `internal` 4; block 5 on `[5]` issued to 2. -/
def h17p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2]
/-- State reached by `h17p` under `KF45` (§57). -/
def h17 : LState := final KF45 [] h17p

/-- **H17** (material §1 C, class Lib). `free` of an arena block. Expected (material): `reject`.
Obtained: `reject`, even with the region declared deallocable: the leaf 5 is a part of the storage,
not an `OwnedRoot` (§70.1; §9: subplaces returned by an arena are not new allocations). Twin: after
the end of the block (`endUse` of its value), `free` of the allocated storage 4 is `ok`. -/
theorem H17 : RunsTo KF45 [] h17p h17 ∧ FreeStep KF45 5 7 h17.kern .reject ∧
    ¬ OwnedRoot h17.kern 5 ∧ Runs KF45 [] (h17p ++ [.endUse 2, .free 4 7]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-! ## D. Arenas -/

/-- State reached by `h17p` under `K0` (§57). -/
def h18 : LState := final K0 [] h17p

/-- **H18** (material §1 D, class Lib). The arena value transferred into a block of its own
storage. Expected (material): `reject`. Obtained: `reject`: §63.8 fails, `internal` (the root of
the storage, held by the arena value) would be held by `corr(0) = 5` and covers the leaf 5 (§40,
§88); §63.6 fails as well, the storage becoming owned by its own leaf (no frame for the anchor of
the value 2). Twin: the transfer of the arena value into the local leaf 3 is `ok`. -/
theorem H18 : RunsTo K0 [] h17p h18 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 5 h18.kern .reject ∧
    ¬ NoLocalSelfLock h18.kern 0 5 ∧ Runs K0 [] (h17p ++ [.transfer 0 3]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H19 (§76, §77): storage 4 (leaf 5) owned by the arena value 0; parent arena on 4; block
5 on `[5]` issued to 2; child arena on the leaf 5 with `internal` the block 5, its arena value 2. -/
def h19o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 4],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 4 4, .issue 0 [5] 2, .newArena 5 5]
/-- State reached by `h19o` (§57). -/
def h19 : LState := final K0 [] h19o

/-- **H19** (material §1 D, class Lib). Nested arena: `reset` of the parent while the child
lives, then after `endUse` of the child value. Expected (material): `reject`, then `ok`. Obtained:
`reject` (§78.2: the child's `internal`, block 5, is active and covers leaf 5), then `ok` (§69
effect releases it; §78). -/
theorem H19 : RunsTo K0 [] h19o h19 ∧ ResetD 0 h19 .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] (h19o ++ [.endUse 2, .reset 0]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (k := K0) (o := .reset 0) (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- **H20** (material §1 D, class Lib). `alloc`, `newArena`, `issue`, `endUse`, `reset`, then
`issue` of the same region. Expected (material): all `ok`. Obtained: all `ok` (§76–§78, §46,
§86). -/
theorem H20 : Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3],
    .write 0 [0], .newArena 3 3, .issue 0 [4] 2, .endUse 2, .reset 0, .issue 0 [4] 2] :=
  runsTo (by decide)

/-- Test contract of H21 (§68.1, §80): the arena value 0 is `SharedMutable`. -/
abbrev KA : K := KD.toK { shared := [0] }

/-- Prefix of H21 (§71, §76): frame 1 with arena value 0, allocator 1, buffer 2; storage 3
(leaves 4, 5) owned by 0; arena on 3 with `internal` 3. -/
def h21p : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 1 [1], .alloc 1 0 [lf, pt 3, pt 3],
  .write 0 [0], .newArena 3 3]
/-- Run of H21 (§60, §72, §68): the caller passes 4, `Observe` on the arena value, and 5,
`Modify` on its buffer; the callee (local 6) updates the arena metadata by `writeShared`. -/
def h21o : List Op := h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .observe, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
  .writeShared 4 [0]]
/-- State reached by `h21o` (§57). -/
def h21 : LState := final KA [] h21o

/-- **H21** (material §1 D, class Lib). A callee that only observes the arena issues a block to a
local, then returns the block. Expected (material): `ok`. Obtained: the `writeShared` on the
metadata is `ok` (§68), but the `issue` is `reject`: `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` on
the arena value and `writeShared` alone does not satisfy it (§36, §77.1). Twin, the same run with a
`Modify` parameter on the arena value: `issue`, `transfer` of the block value to the caller and
`exitFrame` are `ok`. **MISMATCH** (expected `ok`, obtained `reject`); cause: spec change (§36,
§77.1). -/
theorem H21 : RunsTo KA [] h21o h21 ∧ IssueD KA 0 [4] 6 h21 .reject ∧
    OptP (h21.arenas[0]?) (fun E => ¬ MetaRight h21.kern E) False ∧
    Runs KA [] (h21p ++ [.derive 0 [0] .modify, .derive 2 [2] .modify, .enter [4, 5] [lf],
      .writeShared 4 [0], .issue 0 [4] 6, .transfer 6 2, .exit]) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), rejects (o := .issue 0 [4] 6) (by decide), by decide, runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H21b (§72, §60, §65, §76): frame 1 with the result 0 passes 1, `Modify` on it, to
frame 2, which has the arena value 1 and the local buffer 2 (parts 3, 4); the callee derives 4,
`Modify` on the buffer, stores it into the arena value and creates the arena. -/
def h21bo : List Op := [.enter [] [lf], .derive 0 [0] .modify,
  .enter [1] [lf, lf, pt 2, pt 2], .derive 3 [3, 4] .modify, .store 4 1, .newArena 2 4]
/-- State reached by `h21bo` (§57). -/
def h21b : LState := final K0 [] h21bo

/-- **H21b** (material §1 D, class Lib). An arena on a local buffer, transferred to the caller.
Expected (material): `reject` at the `transfer`. Obtained: `reject`: `internal`, moved to the
caller's place with its anchor, has its effective anchor on the callee's local buffer, so §63.6
(`AnchorOrder`) and §63.7 (`AnchorOrderHeld`) fail in the resulting state (§44, §79). Twin
(material pairing): `H37`, the arena on an allocated storage owned by its value, is `ok`. -/
theorem H21b : RunsTo K0 [] h21bo h21b ∧ TransferStep K0 1 0 h21b.kern .reject ∧
    ¬ AnchorOrderHeld (transferEff h21b.kern 1 0) :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), by decide⟩

/-! ## E. Pinning and static storage -/

/-- Run of H22 (§72, §74): frame 1 with `x` (0), written and pinned, and `y` (1). -/
def h22o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .pin 0]
/-- State reached by `h22o` (§57). -/
def h22 : LState := final K0 [] h22o

/-- **H22** (material §1 E, class N3). Transfer of a value whose in-place leaf is pinned / of a
value whose owned storage only is pinned. Expected (material): `reject` / `ok`. Obtained:
`reject` (§63.5) / `ok` (§63.5: owned storage not moved does not prevent the transfer; §87). Twin
of the rejection, without the pin: `ok`. -/
theorem H22 : RunsTo K0 [] h22o h22 ∧ TransferStep K0 0 1 h22.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .transfer 0 1] ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf, lf, lf], .write 0 [0], .write 1 [1], .alloc 0 1 [lf], .pin 3,
      .transfer 1 2] :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Run of H23 (§72, §74): frame 1 calls frame 2, whose local 1 is pinned. -/
def h23o : List Op := [.enter [] [lf], .enter [] [lf], .pin 1]
/-- State reached by `h23o` (§57). -/
def h23 : LState := final K0 [] h23o

/-- **H23** (material §1 E, class N3). Exit of a frame whose local is pinned. Expected (material):
`reject`. Obtained: `reject` (§73.3). Twin without the pin: `ok`. -/
theorem H23 : RunsTo K0 [] h23o h23 ∧ ExitStep K0 h23.kern .reject ∧
    Runs K0 [] [.enter [] [lf], .enter [] [lf], .exit] :=
  ⟨runsTo (by decide), .reject (by decide), runsTo (by decide)⟩

/-- Statics of H24 (§47): the MMIO leaf 0, `Init`, and the leaf 1, `Uninit`. -/
def stM : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false)]
/-- Test contract of H24 (§74, §75, §80): the static leaf 0 is `K.Pinned`. -/
